memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The man who is clean is to sprinkle those who are unclean on the third and seventh days, and on the seventh day he is to purify them. Those who are being cleansed must wash their clothes and bathe with water, and that evening they will be clean. But if those who are unclean do not purify themselves, they must be cut off from the community, because they have defiled the sanctuary of the Lord. The water of cleansing has not been sprinkled on them, and they are unclean." — Num 19:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The purpose of all this cleansing becomes clear here: to restore the unclean person to the community and to God's presence. Those who refused the cleansing would be "cut off," separated from God's people and His sanctuary. Cleansing was not an optional extra; it was the way back into fellowship. Without it, a person remained on the outside.

This shows us that cleansing is ultimately about relationship. God did not provide the water of cleansing merely to satisfy a rule, but to bring His people back into nearness with Him. The whole point was restoration — being able to draw near to the living God and dwell among His people again. Purity opened the door to communion.

The sobering side is that cleansing had to be received. The provision was there, freely available, but a person had to actually be sprinkled with the water. To refuse it was to remain unclean and cut off. God's grace does not force itself upon us; it must be received.

This carries a gentle but serious invitation for us. God has provided complete cleansing in Christ, fully sufficient for every sin and stain. But it must be received by faith. To turn away from Christ is to remain in our uncleanness, separated from God. Yet to come to Him is to be washed, restored, and welcomed near. The purpose has never changed: God cleanses us so that we may draw near to Him. He does not want us cut off; He longs to bring us home. Will you receive the cleansing He so freely offers?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you see cleansing as being ultimately about restored relationship with God?
2. Have you personally received the cleansing God offers in Christ?
3. What does it mean that God cleanses you so you can draw near to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your cleansing is all about drawing me near to You. Thank You that in Christ full cleansing is offered to me freely. Help me to receive it by faith, and to live in the joy of restored fellowship with You. Amen.
